title: Checkpoint checksum & index investigation
content:
Quick scratchpad: intermittent model-load failures in staging when pulling v2 checkpoints from GCS. Notes + commands I ran, error snippets, and hypotheses.  

Context:
- Model: 'mosaic-x-14b-finetuned' (internal alias mymodel:v2)
- Deployment: staging-serving-3 (dedicated pool)
- Symptom window: ~2025-02-17 18:30 - 20:45 UTC
- Failure class: loader throws ChecksumMismatchError or EOFError while validating shard index during load. Not a full crash of the node, just model load aborted and fallback to smaller variant.

Symptoms observed (examples):
- logs/serving-runtime.log snippets:
  [2025-02-17T18:41:02Z] ERROR model-loader: shard-3.bin checksum mismatch (expected 2f7d3b..., got 000000...)
  [2025-02-17T18:41:02Z] WARN model-loader: falling back to mymodel:v1 (smaller)
  [2025-02-17T19:10:12Z] ERROR model-loader: EOFError while reading index.json (read 0 bytes)
  [2025-02-17T19:10:12Z] DEBUG gcs-fetch: retrying download (attempt 2)

Commands I ran locally/on staging node (order matters):
1) quick sizes + sha checks on GCS objects
  gsutil ls -l gs://redwood-checkpoints/mymodel/v2/*
  gsutil stat gs://redwood-checkpoints/mymodel/v2/checkpoint.tar.gz
  gsutil cp gs://redwood-checkpoints/mymodel/v2/checkpoint.tar.gz /tmp/ && sha256sum /tmp/checkpoint.tar.gz
  # result: checksum matched expected manifest (manifest SHA: 2f7d3b...). But extracting gave weird file sizes for some shards.

2) inspect tarball contents and extract list:
  tar -tvf /tmp/checkpoint.tar.gz | head -n 40\  # shows shards: shard-0.bin ... shard-7.bin, index.json, manifest.json

3) extract single shard and verify header/lengths:
  mkdir -p /tmp/cp_check && tar -xOf /tmp/checkpoint.tar.gz shards/shard-3.bin > /tmp/cp_check/shard-3.bin\  ls -lh /tmp/cp_check/shard-3.bin && sha256sum /tmp/cp_check/shard-3.bin
  # observed: size 0B for one extract attempt on later re-download -> suggests tar read returned truncated member under some conditions

4) compare multiple downloads to rule out transient network truncation:
  for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do gsutil cp gs://redwood-checkpoints/mymodel/v2/checkpoint.tar.gz /tmp/checkpoint-$i.tar.gz && sha256sum /tmp/checkpoint-$i.tar.gz; done
  # all checksums equal in 3/5 runs; 2 runs produced smaller file and sha256 was different -> indicates intermittent incomplete reads from GCS endpoint for that VM/zone

5) low-level byte inspection on problematic file:
  xxd -l 64 /tmp/checkpoint-bad.tar.gz | sed -n '1,10p'
  # header cut off mid-tar header in bad file. Matches EOFError on loader when reading inside tar member.

6) used gsutil -D cp (debug) to see retries and errors. Found 'Read aborted' messages at network layer on staging VMs with older kernel (amazonec2 m6g?)

7) validated object MD5/CRC32 via gcs API vs sha256 from manifest: gcloud storage objects describe returned md5Hash/sizeMatches, but our manifest uses sha256. GCS CRC/MD5 passed when file complete; truncated downloads gave mismatched size so API still show object size correct.

Local reproduction attempt (small script to stream-read tar members to catch header failures):
  python - <<'PY'
import tarfile,sys
for p in ['/tmp/checkpoint-1.tar.gz','/tmp/checkpoint-bad.tar.gz']:
    try:
        with tarfile.open(p,'r:gz') as t:
            for m in t:
                print(p,m.name,m.size)
    except Exception as e:
        print('ERR',p,e)
PY
  # Good file enumerates; bad file raises ReadError: file could not be opened successfully

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Network/VM-level intermittent truncated reads from GCS due to MTU/kernel/drivers (most likely). Evidence: repeated cp sometimes returns smaller file; xxd shows truncated tar header. Some staging instances on older AMI/kernel reported similar errors in unrelated tickets.
2) Multipart upload on producer side failed during rollout (incomplete tar uploaded but manifest published). Less likely because object metadata size in GCS equals expected and multiple downloads sometimes succeed. Would expect persistent failure if upload corrupt.
3) Bug in our streaming GCS client that returns EOF prematurely under certain backpressure patterns (possible; we recently updated http client lib).
4) Checksum comparison expects SHA256 in manifest but sometimes we only verify MD5/CRC returned by GCS; mismatch in verification logic could mark good objects as bad (less consistent with logs showing actual truncated bytes).
5) Checkpoint format change: v2 introduced per-shard compressed blocks; loader fails when encountering unexpected magic. Could explain BadMagicNumber errors occasionally.

What fixed or mitigations tried so far:
- temporarily pinned staging nodes to newer AMI with updated kernel (migrations on 3 nodes). After that, observed no truncation on those nodes for 24h.
- added extra retry wrapper around gsutil copy in startup bootstrap (additional 3 attempts + sleep). Reduced flakiness but didn't eliminate.
- disabled on-the-fly streaming extraction in loader and instead download full tarball to disk before extract on nodes with flaky network (workaround). High disk IO cost, but prevents partial extraction EOF.
- added extra validation: after download, compare sha256 against manifest before attempting load. Prevents partial-load, makes failure explicit earlier.

Open next steps / todo:
- [ ] Run controlled experiment: spin 10 instances on older AMI vs 10 on new AMI, repeatedly download 1000x and collect statistics (download size, sha256 mismatch, tcp retransmits). Ticket: INF-3490
- [ ] Instrument GCS client in loader to log Content-Length header vs bytes received + record any early EOFs with stack trace (low-effort).
- [ ] Ask infra to check NAT gateway logs for partial connection resets around failure times.
- [ ] Have release/ops check whether producer pipeline ever did multipart uploads with ephemeral interruptions (ping data team).
- [ ] Consider switching manifest verification to use GCS MD5/CRC in addition to SHA256 for faster early reject.

Notes for postmortem / what to capture if this hits production:
- capture exact object name + generation id from GCS (so we can confirm server-side object integrity)
- collect VM kernel version, kernel dmesg, iptables/nat timeouts, and gcs client debug logs (gsutil -D)
- preserve a copy of the corrupted tarball (don't overwrite) and run file/xxd/tar -tvf on it as evidence
- timeline: when manifest was published vs when object generation created (race conditions?)

Misc quick heuristics I scribbled while debugging:
- if sha256 matches manifest -> safe to stream extract
- if tar extracting fails mid-member -> likely truncated download (rarely format bug)
- if loader sees lots of "got 0 bytes" reads repeatedly -> check socket read timeout, kernel, NIC drivers

Conclusion (current): most evidence points to intermittent truncated reads from certain staging VMs causing tar members to be incomplete, which surfaces as checksum mismatch / EOF. Short-term: pin AMI + full-download-then-validate. Medium-term: instrument client, run VM comparison experiment, and coordinate with infra team to identify root cause.

Logs and small outputs attached in linked_artifacts above and in /mnt/experiments/nina/checksum-investigation/ (on my laptop)

Notes-to-self: convert this into a proper incident writeup if we reproduce on prod or if INF-3421 gets escalated.
